title: Every owner uses ei ole
focus: Negative possession uses the same ei ole with every owner: minulla ei ole, sinulla ei ole, hänellä ei ole, meillä ei ole, teillä ei ole, heillä ei ole.

exercises.prompt: Choose “He does not have a car.” in Finnish. Use hänellä (“he as the owner”) and autoa (“a car”). Frame: “Hänellä ___ autoa”.
exercises.explanation: Use fixed ei ole with every possessor. The owner does not change the negative verb to en, emme, or eivät.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed ei ole in possession: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.translation: He does not have a car.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: hän has the learned possession form hänellä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with every owner; do not change it to en, emme, or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
auto + -a = autoa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed ei ole in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
